lines.trans: Is this normal? Your waiter wanted to overcharge me!
Do you value your reputation at all?
She is the one who served me.
No, well this is some kind of mistake!
I was simply framed!
I beg your pardon, we will sort this out right now.
I apologize, I am the owner of this mess.
Did something happen? They tried to overcharge me.
You are fired. Shut your mouth and hand in your badge.
Our life is always the result of our choice.
We choose to tell the truth or to keep silent.
Or to turn everything into a joke that you will remember for a long time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы вообще дорожите своей репутацией?

examples.text: Вы вообще дорожите своей репутацией?
examples.trans: Do you value your reputation at all?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и дорожить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and value on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Not only did she almost run me over, she also insulted me.

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will sort this out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.

examples.text: Я скоро во всём разберусь.
examples.trans: I'll figure everything out soon.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'виняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'apologize'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и извиняться вовремя.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют извиняться.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'owner' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: to try, to attempt, to make an effort

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты что делаешь? Заказал просто кофе!
examples.trans: What are you doing? He ordered just coffee!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'воленный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fired').

examples.text: Вы все уволены.

examples.text: Ты не уволена, я просто пошутила.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'close', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: Вёз взятку в институт, а он сам сессию закрыл.

examples.text: Закрой дверь, пожалуйста.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что самое важное в работе официанта?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'name badge' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты уволена. Рот закрой и бейджик сдай.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our, ours', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'result' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Наша жизнь — это всегда результат нашего выбора.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'choice' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We need to do everything and to keep silent on time.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn into', paired with 'превращать'.

examples.text: Или превратить всё в шутку, о которой будешь долго вспоминать.
examples.trans: Or to turn everything into a joke that you will remember for a long time.

examples.text: Они умеют превратить работу в праздник.
examples.trans: They know how to turn work into a holiday.

examples.text: Дети умеют превратить работу в праздник.
examples.trans: Children know how to turn work into a holiday.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И всё.
examples.trans: And that is all.

examples.text: Всё. До свидания.
examples.trans: That is all. Goodbye.

examples.text: Но штуку я всё равно выиграл.
examples.trans: But I still won a grand anyway.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что самое важное в работе официанта?
examples.trans: What is the most important thing in a waiter's job?

examples.text: Манеры? Вежливость?
examples.trans: Manners? Politeness?

examples.text: Эффектная подача блюд делает их вкуснее.
examples.trans: Spectacular presentation of dishes makes them tastier.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'joke' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас появился ещё один шутник.
examples.trans: We have got ourselves another prankster.

examples.text: Или превратить всё в шутку, о которой будешь долго вспоминать.
examples.trans: Or to turn everything into a joke that you will remember for a long time.

examples.text: Это шутка.
examples.trans: It's a joke.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Что самое важное в работе официанта?
examples.trans: What is the most important thing in a waiter's job?

examples.text: Манеры? Вежливость?
examples.trans: Manners? Politeness?

examples.text: Эффектная подача блюд делает их вкуснее.
examples.trans: Spectacular presentation of dishes makes them tastier.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who, which (relative)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ребёнку необходимы белки, которые есть только в мясе.
examples.trans: A baby needs proteins that are only in meat.

examples.text: Я добавила ингредиент, который вы в шкафчик мне подкинули.
examples.trans: I added the ingredient that you planted in my locker.

examples.text: Дима просил приготовить блюдо, которое он в обед ел с вырезкой.
examples.trans: Dima asked to prepare the dish with tenderloin that he ate at lunch.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will'.

examples.text: Шеф, дорогой, для тебя я могу быть кем угодно.
examples.trans: Chef, my dear friend, for you I can be anyone at all.

examples.text: Она должна быть, во-первых, свежей.
examples.trans: First of all, it must be fresh.

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мне дали пятнашку, а я должен забрать семь?
examples.trans: They gave me fifteen, and I have to take seven?

examples.text: Почему я должен работать на ушастых?
examples.trans: Why do I have to work for big-eared rookies?

examples.text: Она должна быть, во-первых, свежей.
examples.trans: First of all, it must be fresh.

meanings.en: to recall, to try to remember, to reminisce
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'поминать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to remember, look back on', paired with 'вспомнить'.

examples.text: Или превратить всё в шутку, о которой будешь долго вспоминать.
examples.trans: Or to turn everything into a joke that you will remember for a long time.

examples.text: Я так вспоминаю.
examples.trans: I'm trying to recall it.

examples.text: Я так вспоминаю. Значит, машину разбил, что ли?
examples.trans: I'm trying to recall it. So I wrecked the car, then?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'time' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Время покажет наш выбор!
examples.trans: Time will show our choice!

examples.text: У меня нет времени.
examples.trans: I don't have time.

examples.text: Мы хорошо проводим время.
examples.trans: We're having a good time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.text: Покажите руки!
examples.trans: Show me your hands!

examples.text: Покажем это Аникееву?
examples.trans: Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?
